relevant_findings.meaning: Electron userData is explicitly set during bootstrap from appData/buildFlavor/env-derived logic.
Packaged app uses Electron single-instance locking and exits second desktop instance when lock fails.
Second-instance args are queued into the primary process, which can collapse an intended isolated launch into an existing app instance.
Desktop can select bundled or env-overridden Codex CLI path for certain runtime/tool surfaces.
CODEX_HOME is propagated into node_repl MCP/server environment, not sufficient by itself for all Electron/macOS storage.
Webview helper logic treats CODEX_HOME or HOME/.codex as Codex home for worktree classification.

negative_findings.result: No direct string hit in JS scan; prior launch used Chromium/Electron CLI arg successfully but it did not isolate all macOS bundle-id storage.
No safe supported bypass identified in read-only scan.

conclusion: ASAR scan supports a future copied/renamed bundle dry-run because bundle identity/userData/single-instance behavior are central. It does not support official app env-wrapper as safe enough.
